You will have up to 10 minutes to make your presentation to the judge (you may have more than one judge). You will be evaluated on how well you demonstrate the 21st Century Skills and meet the performance indicators of this event. Turn in all of your notes and event materials when you have completed the event.
situation:
You are the operations coordinator at CURBSIDE COAT GROOMING, a mobile pet grooming business owned by the six groomers who work in it. Every member holds an equal share, every major spending decision goes to a vote of the members, and any profit left at year end is paid out to them. The member-chair (judge) runs those meetings and has asked you to bring a recommendation to the next one.

Two vans serve about two hundred households, most of them clients who cannot easily drive a dog across town to a salon. Two years ago the co-op signed a two-year agreement with a regional senior services agency, holding half of every week's appointment slots for that agency's clients at a reduced rate. Those appointments are steady, they rebook, and the booking records show they almost never cancel.

A regional pitch competition is now open. The winner receives a fifty thousand dollar grant, enough for a third van and the equipment to fit it out. The application asks entrants to apply their own booking information to a growth plan, and the grant is paid out only if the winner adds a set number of new suburban clients within twelve months.

The co-op cannot serve those new suburban clients and still hold half of every week's slots for the senior services agency; the agreement has ten months left to run. The alternative is to skip the competition and buy the third van out of the members' own earnings instead, which would take about three years and mean no year-end payout to the members in the meantime.

The member-chair (judge) wants you to analyze what the booking records actually show, weigh the grant against the commitment already made to the agency, and recommend whether the co-op should enter the competition. The member-chair (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas, ask two questions, and thank you when the presentation and questions are over.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the member-chair of CURBSIDE COAT GROOMING. Business background is the same as the situation above. You groom alongside the other five members, you chaired the meeting that approved the agreement with the regional senior services agency, and you will have to put whatever the co-op decides to a vote. A third van is the only way the business grows, and the pitch competition is the fastest route to one.

You have asked the operations coordinator (participant) to analyze what the booking records show, weigh the fifty thousand dollar grant against the commitment already made to the agency, and recommend whether the co-op should enter the competition. You want to understand what the members would be giving up under either course before you take it to a vote.

After the participant has presented, you will ask these two questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would tell us early that it was going wrong?
